mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate general partner's board of directors or equivalent governing body

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed general partner or authorized officer

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all general partners, limited partners, 25% UBOs, authorized representatives, and, where applicable, client counterparties against: the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act; United Nations Security Council sanctions lists implemented under the United Nations Act; the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for USD-clearing transactions; the UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions list; the EU consolidated sanctions list; and FATF public statements. Politically exposed persons, including domestic and foreign heads of state, parliamentarians, deputies, judges, military leaders, and senior public-office holders, require enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and 12-month post-exit monitoring. Adverse-media and source-of-funds verification must be completed before name reservation and maintained throughout the entity's life.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) for federal name reservation; provincial/territorial limited partnership registries, such as the Ontario Business Registry or applicable provincial equivalent, complete the LP name clearance after a NUANS name search report is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the official-languages framework and federal/provincial corporate nomenclature rules, the legal name may be in English, French, or bilingual form. A non-Latin-script name must be transliterated into Latin characters, and that transliteration becomes the enumerated name for registration. The name must be distinguishable from existing federal and provincial registrations; the statutory designation 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'société en commandite', or 'S.E.C.' must appear when required by the applicable limited partnership legislation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file additional alternative names on the same NUANS report during its validity period, or request reconsideration in writing to Corporations Canada or the applicable provincial registrar within 30 days of rejection, furnishing evidence of distinguishability and, where necessary, written consent from the holder of a competing name. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may apply for judicial review to the Federal Court of Canada under section 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-7, or to the applicable provincial superior court, within 30 days of the final administrative decision. Where the reservation is about to expire, a renewal filing must be submitted before expiry; no renewal is permitted after the original reservation window lapses without a fresh NUANS search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional and limited. A virtual-office or registered-agent address is acceptable solely for service of process and statutory correspondence. It is not sufficient as the exclusive operational premises for an actual federal/provincial government-affairs lobbying and advisory business. CRA and the applicable lobbying registrar may challenge a nominal address if no Canadian physical presence, decision-making function, staff, or operational records support the partnership's asserted residence and commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10-15% aggregate risk in the first year of an announced tax, GST/HST, or provincial audit visit; unannounced physical inspections are uncommon for limited partnerships but may rise to 25% or more where the entity registers as a consultant lobbyist, receives foreign-principal funding, or is selected for an enhanced substance or anti-money-laundering examination.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended, ss. 5(1), 6(1), 9(2), 102(1), 114(1); Canada Partnerships Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. P-3, s. 2(1) (governance gap)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Director, Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Limited Partnership together with Declaration of General Partner
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the CBCA or applicable federal partnership regulations. The limited partners' contributions are contractually fixed in the Limited Partnership Agreement and may be satisfied by cash, property, or services. No statutory escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation of the Limited Partnership (the 'LP') under the Canada Business Corporations Act is hereby ratified, and the General Partner subscribes for the limited partnership units set forth in the subscription agreement; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the LP be established at the address specified in the Articles; RESOLVED, that the individuals named in the officer appointment schedule be and are hereby appointed as the General Partner's officers and agents with full authority to execute filings and open bank accounts; RESOLVED, that the General Partner is authorized to take all necessary actions to complete registration under the Lobbying Act and open operating bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online portal via nuans.com
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS pre-approved name search for the proposed limited partnership name. Submit a name reservation request through the Corporations Canada e-filing interface. Provide a succinct business description and designate the jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusing or not distinctive, file a revised name request through the same portal, incorporating the examiner's objections, within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Formation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Limited Partnership counsel and federal registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Limited Partnership, Declaration of General Partner, Limited Partnership Agreement, and the General Partner's board resolution. Execute all documents in counterparts and ensure each partner acknowledges the prescribed statutory declarations.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Registered Office (Form 11)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries document inconsistencies, rectify the execution pages, refile with the Director, and correct the questioned provisions via a certificate of correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to Corporations Canada and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Director, Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles of Limited Partnership and Declaration of General Partner through the Corporations Canada e-filing portal, pay the prescribed fee, and await issuance of the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or queried, respond through the Corporations Canada contact centre within 21 days, provide the missing statutory particulars, and obtain a reinstated application or revised certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Federal Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Limited Partnership, register the LP and its General Partner with the CRA through the Business Registration Online (BRO) system to obtain a Business Number (BN), GST/HST program account, and payroll account for any partner-employees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA requests additional partnership details, provide the Limited Partnership Agreement and partner allocation percentages via the BRO document upload, and request manual verification within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lobbying Act Registration and Local Licensing Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying of Canada; municipal occupational health offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a lobbyist registration in the federal Registry of Lobbyists naming the LP as the registrant, the client, and the subject matter (cross-border trade policy and foreign stakeholder lobbying). Obtain fire safety inspection, structural occupancy approval, and workplace clearance from the local authority having jurisdiction.
required_dossiers: Completed Lobbyists Registration Form (for ongoing engagement)
Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) compliance self-audit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is rejected due to incomplete subject matter details, amend the registry submission and provide the relevant machine-readable policy documents to the Office of the Commissioner within 15 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying of Canada (federal lobbying regulator); municipal business licensing division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Federal Lobbyist Registration Certificate (Class: Consultant/In-house Lobbyist)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category IV (non-industrial administrative and advisory operations)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial wastewater discharge; municipal sewer discharge limited to 50 m³/day. VOC emissions less than 0.5 tonnes per year. Hazardous waste handling capped at 5 kg/month. Full compliance with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 Schedule 5 and the Fisheries Act s.36(3).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification obtained from the local fire marshal meeting National Fire Code of Canada standards; structural load certificate for office floor loading (minimum 6.0 kPa); workplace clearance under the Canada Labour Code Part II and applicable provincial occupational health and safety regulations; completing all employee WHMIS and emergency-response training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal tax authority; administrative portal is CRA My Business Account and the Non-Resident Registration service via https://www.canada.ca/taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and, if taxable supplies exceed the threshold, a GST/HST account (RT0001). Procedure: (1) appoint a named representative or contact in Canada; (2) file Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' or use the CRA non-resident online registration module; (3) provide the partnership agreement, foreign registration certificate, and the Canadian representative's name and address; (4) receive the 9-digit BN with applicable program accounts (RT for GST/HST, RC for payroll if applicable); (5) alternatively, a foreign LP may file Form RC459 'GST/HST Registration for Non-Residents'. CRA processing generally completes within 15-30 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — limited partnerships are fiscally transparent under Income Tax Act s. 96 (income and loss flow through to partners), but for GST/HST purposes the partnership is treated as a distinct 'person' under Excise Tax Act s. 123(1) and must file its own GST/HST returns; territorial scope: non-resident partners are taxable only on Canadian-source income under ITA ss. 2(3) and 115; no tax-exempt zone treatment applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canada; partnership transparency is mandatory. Available elections: fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1(3) to adopt a non-calendar partnership taxation year; voluntary GST/HST registration election under ETA s. 240(1) where the partnership is a small supplier; ETA s. 156 election to zero-rate certain supplies between related participating registrants; hybrid-mismatch rules in the Income Tax Act implementing OECD BEPS Action 2 apply to deny double-non-taxation where a Canadian LP is also treated as opaque in a foreign jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / provincial Harmonized Sales Tax) levied under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — mandatory registration is triggered once the partnership's worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or over the four most recent consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold); supplies of services to non-residents are included in the threshold calculation unless zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: CRA does not require real-time fiscal clearance, pre-approval, or digital stamping of invoices. E-invoicing is mandated only for federal B2G suppliers who must transmit invoices through the Pan-Canadian PEPPOL network when contractually required. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary under the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Framework. A GST/HST registrant must issue prescribed invoices showing the business number, GST/HST registration number, and supply description; books and records must be retained for 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Government-affairs advisory and lobbying services qualify for 0% GST/HST under ETA s. 23(1) where the supply is made to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST, the service is not rendered while the non-resident is physically present in Canada, the service does not relate to real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, and the service is not in respect of a business carried on by the non-resident in Canada. Goods physically exported by the partnership may be zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI (ETA s. 1) where export occurs within prescribed timeframes and evidence of export is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) or G7 Export Reporting System record for goods shipped to the United States
Commercial invoice, bill of lading / airway bill, and customs cargo control document proving physical export
For services: signed advisory/retainer contract, contemporaneous narrative and time records, and foreign-client payment evidence (bank credit advice, SWIFT advice, or inward remittance certificate)
GST/HST return and working papers identifying zero-rated supplies (Line 103) and citing the applicable section of the Excise Tax Act
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no explicit statutory FX-repatriation deadline; however, CRA auditors will deny zero-rating where payment is absent or unduly delayed beyond reasonable commercial terms, with a 180-day benchmark applied in this dossier. Consequences of a failed zero-rating claim: GST/HST reassessment with interest; penalty under ETA s. 280 equal to the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the overstated net tax (50% for knowing participation); s. 285.01 false-statement penalties; and the normal 4-year reassessment period is extended up to 10 years where misrepresentation or neglect is established. Criminal prosecution may arise for wilful evasion or fraud under the Excise Tax Act and Criminal Code, and lobbying compliance failures can additionally trigger disqualification or penalties under the federal Lobbying Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), exercising issuance, monetary policy, and financial-stability mandates, with the Department of Finance Canada and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as ancillary authorities for currency policy, financial sanctions, and AML/CFT oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a fully free-floating and fully convertible currency regime with no exchange-control legislation in force; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951 and Canada accepted IMF Article VIII obligations in 1952. Current-account and capital-account transactions, including partnership capital contributions, accumulated income repatriation, and profit distributions to non-resident limited partners, are unrestricted and require no central-bank approval or conversion licence. The only structural constraint is the Investment Canada Act net-benefit review threshold applicable to large acquisitions of control by non-Canadians, which does not apply to treasury transfers, retained-earnings remittances, or advisory retainer settlements for the lobbying partnership.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline on export receipts. The Limited Partnership may retain proceeds in CAD or any foreign currency freely, subject only to general FATF-compliant record-keeping and FINTRAC electronic funds transfer (EFT) reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000 or equivalent).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (integrated treasury and FX desk)
Capital Escrow Account / Corporate Trust Account
Operational Account (Latin American and USD clearing corridor)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility as a supplementary corridor, low viability as a primary relationship. FINTRAC-registered payment service providers and EMIs (e.g., Wise Edge Canada, Payoneer, and other MSB-licensed platforms) may be used for expedited low-value cross-border retainer inflows and contractor disbursements; however, they are not chartered banks, cannot access Payments Canada large-value clearing (LVTS/Real-Time Rail) as direct participants, and will not support structured trade finance or documentary letters of credit. FINTRAC EFT record-keeping and MSB registration must be verified before routing any inbound partnership capital, and the LP must maintain a Tier 1 domestic deposit account as the treasury anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC KYC policy, the bank must identify the general partner, the general partner's controlling individuals, and every limited partner owning 25% or more of the partnership. Remote video-based identity verification is generally accepted for initial CDD at Tier 1 Canadian banks, but a physical or notarially attested sign-off is required for the partnership agreement, for any account with a trust/escrow class, and for the issuance of corporate card mandates when the general partner is a newly formed entity; in practice, Tier 1 commercial banking centres require one in-person officer meeting or a certified true-copy document bundle from a notary public in the applicable provincial jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited-partnership beneficial-ownership opacity, including silent limited partners holding an indirect economic interest.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current limited-partnership registration summary from the applicable provincial registry (Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta, or Quebec), executed deed of limited partnership enumerating all partners, a 25%-and-greater ownership attestation, a FINTRAC beneficial-ownership information (BOI) declaration signed by the general partner, and notarized passport copies of ultimate natural-person principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Government-affairs and lobbying business classification (ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541820) triggering the Medium-Risk-Enhanced AML tier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Active registration certificate from the Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying of Canada (Lobbyists Registration Act), detailed client engagement letters identifying the advisory scope, organizational charts of principals, and a written service-description memo confirming the LP performs licensed public-policy analysis rather than undisclosed influence activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) indicator or foreign public-official association arising from lobbying counterparts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed PEP self-assessment questionnaire with negative or disclosed results, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations for each partner, sworn statement that no benefit, gift, or advantage will be conferred on public office holders in contravention of the Criminal Code or provincial lobbying statutes, and a board-approved conflict-of-interest and gift policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound cross-border wire from non-resident limited partners into the partnership operating account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Destination-of-funds statement, partnership capital-account ledger, executed capital-commitment letters, wire-beneficiary explanation, proof of economic substance (office lease, payroll records, or advisory contracts), and Investment Canada Act acquisition-review filing confirmation or exemption opinion where capital contribution is structured as an asset acquisition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate third-party retainer payments from foreign government-related entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed advisory agreement with onward-disbursement schedule, invoices mapping services to agreed milestones, underlying lobbying registration returns, and FINTRAC large-cash-or-EFT reporting forms filed concurrently with account activation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partnership capital injections from non-resident limited partners must be routed via SWIFT MT103 through the LP's Tier 1 Canadian correspondent banking network, using the partnership's designated USD or CAD account at its primary bank; recommended intermediary routing is via the bank's US correspondent (e.g., JPMorgan Chase or Wells Fargo) through Fedwire or CHIPS, with conversion into CAD executed at the bank's commercial spot rate. The wire narrative must state 'LP capital contribution — investment', include a unique partnership identifier, and be accompanied by a source-of-funds letter from the remitting partner to satisfy FINTRAC EFT record-keeping (mandatory for transactions at or above CAD 10,000). No Bank of Canada approval is required; however, the LP should verify the remitting jurisdiction is not a sanctioned jurisdiction under the Special Economic Measures Act or United Nations Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic retainer and operational disbursements clear through Payments Canada Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batch payments and through the Real-Time Rail for high-value or time-critical obligations; cross-border retainer, advisory, and sub-contractor payments clear via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with UN/EDIFACT-style purpose narratives, while larger procurement settlements (if the LP expands into trade-policy logistics consulting) may use SWIFT MT700 documentary letters of credit or MT760 standby letters of credit confirmed through the LP's Tier 1 relationship bank. CAD-denominated supplier payments are settled through the Large Value Transfer System, and USD-denominated disbursements are cleared through the bank's US USD clearing account or via Automated Clearing House for volume payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable forward contracts (tenor up to 24 months) transacted under an ISDA or Canadian Master Forward Agreement with a Tier 1 Schedule I bank
CAD/EUR and CAD/GBP deliverable forwards for contracted retainer inflows denominated in Euro or Sterling
Plain-vanilla CAD/USD currency swap agreements used to align the timing of partnership capital calls and distribution waterfalls
Cross-currency basis swaps for matching USD-denominated liabilities with CAD revenue streams
Over-the-counter CAD/USD call spreads or bought FX options (option-premium strategies only, no speculative option writing) to cap conversion costs on uncertain inbound commitments

Non-deliverable forwards are not ordinarily permissible or necessary in the Canadian market because the CAD is an IMF Article VIII freely convertible currency with a liquid onshore deliverable forward curve

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Lobbying Act registration renewal and monthly communication reports
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying of Canada (Lobbyists Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registration expiry occurs 12 months after the effective registration date; an updated renewal registration must be filed before that anniversary. Monthly communication reports are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar month in which lobbying activity occurred.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 25,000 per violation for individuals and CAD 50,000 per violation for corporations; failure to comply may result in suspension of registration and prohibition on lobbying activities. No administrative strike-off applies to the limited partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and T5013 slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal period, the return is due by March 31 of the immediately following calendar year; for a non-calendar-year fiscal period, the return is due within five months after the end of the fiscal period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty under Income Tax Act section 162(7) of CAD 25 per day per return, with a minimum penalty of CAD 100 and a maximum of CAD 2,500; additional penalties may apply for incomplete T5013 slips. No administrative strike-off of the limited partnership arises from CRA late filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act for a federally incorporated corporate general partner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation of the corporate general partner.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual return for one year may lead to administrative dissolution of the corporate general partner under the CBCA; reinstatement is possible after filing arrears and paying applicable fees, but the general partner's capacity would be interrupted during dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit is imposed solely by reason of an entity being a limited partnership. Compulsory audit arises where: (i) the LP is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities legislation; (ii) the LP is a tax shelter under the Income Tax Act; (iii) the general partner is a federal corporation subject to an audit requirement under its shareholders or regulator; or (iv) the limited partnership agreement, lender, or investment advisers impose an audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable entities; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for ordinary private limited partnerships; tax allocations reported on the T5013 follow the partnership accounting method selected under CRA rules and must be applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A limited partnership is not a CBCA distinct entity and is not subject to the federal Register of Individuals with Significant Control. Annual UBO confirmation is triggered by any transfer, contribution, or withdrawal of partnership interests; the general partner must update the partnership register within 15 days of such changes. If the general partner is a federally incorporated entity, it must maintain its own ISC register and update it for changes in significant control. For FINTRAC AML compliance, the LP must confirm beneficial ownership annually or upon any triggering event with its financial institution.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (name, contribution, withdrawal records)
Minute Book / resolution records of the general partner
